Schema (the tables most likely to be needed):
code_lookup - Meaning of every coded column in the other tables: code_type (which code list: ORD_STATUS, TIER, REFUND_STATUS, REFUND_REASON, TKT_CATEG, REGION, CHANNEL, DEPT); code_val (the stored code); code_desc (what the code means in words)
cust_master - Customer master record: cust_id (customer id, like C-1002); cust_nm (customer name); tier_cd (loyalty tier: P platinum, G gold, S standard); region_cd (sales region: NA, EU, AP, LA); signup_dt (date the customer signed up); is_actv (1 = active, 0 = closed or inactive (soft delete)); email_addr (contact email address); phone_no (contact phone number)
fx_rate - Exchange rates, one row per currency per effective date: currency_cd (ISO currency code); eff_dt (first date the rate applies); rate_to_usd (multiply an amount in this currency by this to get USD)
ord_hdr - Order header, one row per order: ord_id (order id, like O-5002); cust_id (customer who placed the order); ord_dt (order date); ord_status (N new, S shipped, D delivered, C cancelled, R returned); ord_total_amt (order total in the ORDER currency (currency_cd), already net of line discounts); currency_cd (currency of ord_total_amt); channel_cd (sales channel: WEB, APP, PHN, STR)  FK: cust_id->cust_master.cust_id
refund_req - Refund requests: rfd_id (refund request id, like R-9001); ord_id (order the refund is for); req_dt (date the refund was requested); rfd_amt (amount requested, in the order currency); reason_cd (reason: DMG damaged, DUP duplicate charge, LAT late delivery, OTH other); status_cd (P pending, A approved, D denied); approver_emp_id (employee who decided; NULL while pending); decided_dt (date decided; NULL while pending)  FK: ord_id->ord_hdr.ord_id
support_tkt - Support tickets: tkt_id (ticket id, like T-70010); cust_id (customer who raised the ticket); opened_ts (when the ticket was opened); closed_ts (when it was closed; NULL means the ticket is still open); sev_lvl (severity: 1 critical, 2 high, 3 medium, 4 low); categ_cd (category: BILL billing, SHIP shipping, TECH technical, ACCT account, REFD refunds); assigned_emp_id (employee working it; NULL if not yet assigned); channel_cd (how it arrived: WEB, APP, PHN, STR)  FK: cust_id->cust_master.cust_id
shipment - Shipments, one per shipped order: ship_id (shipment id, like S-8001); ord_id (order shipped); wh_id (warehouse it left from); carrier_cd (carrier: UPS, DHL, FDX, USP); ship_dt (date handed to the carrier); deliv_dt (date delivered; NULL until delivered); ship_status (shipment state: I in transit, D delivered)  FK: ord_id->ord_hdr.ord_id

Show the count of support tickets by severity level for tickets opened in April 2026, ordered by severity level ascending.

```sql

```

A high-lead secondary supplier is any supplier that is not the primary supplier (is_primary = 0) and has a lead time of 20 days or more. Show the supplier name, SKU, and lead days for all high-lead secondary suppliers, ordered by lead days descending, breaking ties by supplier name ascending.

```sql
SELECT s.sup_nm, ps.sku, ps.lead_days FROM supplier s JOIN prod_supplier ps ON s.sup_id = ps.sup_id WHERE ps.is_primary = 0 AND ps.lead_days >= 20 ORDER BY ps.lead_days DESC, s.sup_nm ASC
```

```sql

```

For each warehouse name, compute the total inventory on-hand quantity, the total reorder point sum, and the ratio of total on-hand quantity to total reorder point expressed as a percentage.

```sql
SELECT w.wh_nm, SUM(i.on_hand_qty) AS total_on_hand, SUM(i.reorder_pt) AS total_reorder_pt, (SUM(i.on_hand_qty) * 100.0) / NULLIF(SUM(i.reorder_pt), 0) AS stock_to_reorder_ratio FROM warehouse w JOIN inventory i ON w.wh_id = i.wh_id GROUP BY w.wh_id, w.wh_nm ORDER BY w.wh_nm ASC
```

Find the supplier ID and supplier name for suppliers who provide products in category ELC but do not supply any products in category KIT.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT T1.sup_id, T1.sup_nm FROM supplier AS T1 INNER JOIN prod_supplier AS T2 ON T1.sup_id = T2.sup_id INNER JOIN prod_catalog AS T3 ON T2.sku = T3.sku WHERE T3.categ_cd = 'ELC' AND T1.sup_id NOT IN (SELECT T4.sup_id FROM prod_supplier AS T4 INNER JOIN prod_catalog AS T5 ON T4.sku = T5.sku WHERE T5.categ_cd = 'KIT')
```

Using a recursive CTE, find the full reporting chain under employee E-001, returning the employee ID, full name, and their depth level starting at 1 for direct reports.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE rep_chain AS (SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, 1 AS depth FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id = 'E-001' UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm, rc.depth + 1 FROM emp e JOIN rep_chain rc ON e.mgr_emp_id = rc.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, depth FROM rep_chain ORDER BY depth ASC, emp_id ASC
```

```sql
WITH RankedRefunds AS (SELECT reason_cd, rfd_id, req_dt, rfd_amt, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY reason_cd ORDER BY rfd_amt DESC, rfd_id ASC) as rnk FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND req_dt <= '2025-12-31') SELECT reason_cd, rfd_id, req_dt, rfd_amt FROM RankedRefunds WHERE rnk <= 2 ORDER BY reason_cd ASC, rfd_amt DESC, rfd_id ASC
```

For each month in 2026, find the SKU that generated the highest total line revenue (qty * unit_prc). Use a CTE with ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by month. Show month, SKU, and total revenue, ordered by month.

```sql

```

Calculate the percentage of total inventory value (on-hand quantity multiplied by list price) held in each warehouse compared to the global inventory value. Show the warehouse ID, warehouse name, and percentage, ordered by percentage descending.

```sql
WITH wh_val AS (SELECT i.wh_id, SUM(i.on_hand_qty * p.list_prc) AS val FROM inventory i JOIN prod_catalog p ON i.sku = p.sku GROUP BY i.wh_id), global_val AS (SELECT SUM(val) AS gval FROM wh_val) SELECT w.wh_id, w.wh_nm, (wv.val * 100.0 / g.gval) AS pct FROM wh_val wv JOIN warehouse w ON wv.wh_id = w.wh_id CROSS JOIN global_val g ORDER BY pct DESC, w.wh_id ASC
```


For orders placed between 2026-01-01 and 2026-07-31, find customers whose total order value across this period exceeds 300 USD (using the 2026-01-01 exchange rate). Show the customer name and total USD amount, ordered by total USD amount descending, then customer name ascending.

```sql
SELECT t1.cust_nm, SUM(t2.ord_total_amt * t3.rate_to_usd) FROM cust_master AS t1 INNER JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id INNER JOIN fx_rate AS t3 ON t2.currency_cd = t3.currency_cd WHERE t2.ord_dt BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' AND t3.eff_dt = '2026-01-01' GROUP BY t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm HAVING SUM(t2.ord_total_amt * t3.rate_to_usd) > 300.00 ORDER BY SUM(t2.ord_total_amt * t3.rate_to_usd) DESC, t1.cust_nm ASC
```

Show the warehouse name, product name, on-hand quantity, and reorder point for all inventory items at the 'Singapore Hub' where stock is strictly below the reorder point.

```sql

```

Calculate each order line's line revenue as (qty * unit_prc * (1 - disc_pct / 100)), and then show the cumulative sum of line revenue across all order lines ordered by order ID and line number.

```sql
SELECT ord_id, line_no, (qty * unit_prc * (1 - disc_pct / 100)) as line_rev, SUM(qty * unit_prc * (1 - disc_pct / 100)) OVER (ORDER BY ord_id ASC, line_no ASC) as cumulative_rev FROM ord_line ORDER BY ord_id ASC, line_no ASC
```

Show the delivery quarter (QUARTER) and year for shipments completed in 2026, alongside the average delivery lead time in days (calculated as delivery date minus shipment date), grouped by quarter and ordered chronologically.

```sql

```

Using a recursive CTE, find the full reporting chain path (listing employee IDs) for employee E-007 up to the top of the tree.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE path_cte AS (SELECT emp_id, mgr_emp_id, CAST(emp_id AS CHAR(200)) AS chain FROM emp WHERE emp_id = 'E-007' UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.mgr_emp_id, CONCAT(p.chain, ' -> ', e.emp_id) FROM emp e JOIN path_cte p ON e.emp_id = p.mgr_emp_id) SELECT chain FROM path_cte WHERE mgr_emp_id IS NULL
```


Find the top 2 highest-value orders for each sales region of the customer, showing the region code, customer ID, order ID, and order total amount. Order by region code ascending and order total amount descending.

```sql
SELECT region_cd, cust_id, ord_id, ord_total_amt FROM (SELECT c.region_cd, o.cust_id, o.ord_id, o.ord_total_amt, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.region_cd ORDER BY o.ord_total_amt DESC, o.ord_id ASC) AS rn FROM ord_hdr o JOIN cust_master c ON o.cust_id = c.cust_id) t WHERE rn <= 2 ORDER BY region_cd ASC, ord_total_amt DESC
```

```sql

```


```sql
SELECT t1.promo_id, t1.promo_cd, SUM(t3.ord_total_amt) AS total_revenue FROM promo AS t1 JOIN ord_promo AS t2 ON t1.promo_id = t2.promo_id JOIN ord_hdr AS t3 ON t2.ord_id = t3.ord_id GROUP BY t1.promo_id, t1.promo_cd HAVING SUM(t3.ord_total_amt) > 1000.00 ORDER BY total_revenue DESC, t1.promo_id
```


Find the top 3 inventory items by on-hand quantity for each warehouse, returning warehouse ID, SKU, on_hand_qty, and the assigned row number.

```sql
SELECT wh_id, sku, on_hand_qty, rn FROM (SELECT wh_id, sku, on_hand_qty, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY wh_id ORDER BY on_hand_qty DESC, sku ASC) AS rn FROM inventory) t WHERE rn <= 3 ORDER BY wh_id ASC, rn ASC, sku ASC
```

Using recursion, count how many total descendants (subordinates at any level) each top-level executive has. Show the executive employee ID, full name, and total subordinate count.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE org_tree AS (SELECT emp_id AS top_id, emp_id, mgr_emp_id FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT T1.top_id, T2.emp_id, T2.mgr_emp_id FROM org_tree AS T1 JOIN emp AS T2 ON T2.mgr_emp_id = T1.emp_id) SELECT T3.emp_id, T3.emp_nm, COUNT(T1.emp_id) FROM org_tree AS T1 JOIN emp AS T3 ON T1.top_id = T3.emp_id WHERE T1.emp_id <> T3.emp_id GROUP BY T3.emp_id, T3.emp_nm ORDER BY T3.emp_id
```

For each successful payment in USD, compute the running sum of payment amounts and compare each payment to the next payment amount using lead, returning payment ID, paid timestamp, payment amount, running total, and next payment amount.

```sql
SELECT pay_id, paid_ts, pay_amt, SUM(pay_amt) OVER (ORDER BY paid_ts ASC, pay_id ASC) AS running_total, LEAD(pay_amt, 1) OVER (ORDER BY paid_ts ASC, pay_id ASC) AS next_pay_amt FROM payment WHERE currency_cd = 'USD' AND pay_status = 'S' ORDER BY paid_ts ASC, pay_id ASC
```

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE top_boss AS (SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, mgr_emp_id, emp_id AS top_id FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm, e.mgr_emp_id, tb.top_id FROM emp AS e JOIN top_boss AS tb ON e.mgr_emp_id = tb.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, top_id FROM top_boss ORDER BY top_id, emp_id
```

For each month in 2025, calculate the total revenue generated specifically from electronics (ELC category) products in order lines. Return month and category revenue, ordered by month.

```sql

```

Using a recursive CTE, compute the maximum depth of the reporting hierarchy starting from each top-level manager.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE tree_depth AS (SELECT emp_id AS root_id, emp_id, 0 AS lvl FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT td.root_id, e.emp_id, td.lvl + 1 FROM emp e JOIN tree_depth td ON e.mgr_emp_id = td.emp_id) SELECT root_id, MAX(lvl) FROM tree_depth GROUP BY root_id ORDER BY root_id
```

Calculate the ratio of settled payment amount to total order amount for each order that has at least one settled payment. Show the order ID, total order amount, settled payment amount, and payment-to-order ratio, ordered by ratio descending.

```sql
WITH ord_settled AS (SELECT ord_id, SUM(pay_amt) AS settled_amt FROM payment WHERE pay_status = 'S' GROUP BY ord_id) SELECT h.ord_id, h.ord_total_amt, o.settled_amt, (o.settled_amt / h.ord_total_amt) AS pay_ratio FROM ord_hdr h JOIN ord_settled o ON h.ord_id = o.ord_id ORDER BY pay_ratio DESC, h.ord_id ASC
```

A fully paid order is one where the sum of settled payment amounts equals or exceeds the order total amount. For orders placed in currency USD in the year 2026, show the order id, order total amount, and total settled amount, ordered by order total amount descending, then order id ascending.

```sql
SELECT t1.ord_id, t1.ord_total_amt, SUM(t2.pay_amt) AS settled_amt FROM ord_hdr AS t1 JOIN payment AS t2 ON t1.ord_id = t2.ord_id WHERE t1.currency_cd = 'USD' AND t1.ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND t2.pay_status = 'S' GROUP BY t1.ord_id, t1.ord_total_amt HAVING SUM(t2.pay_amt) >= t1.ord_total_amt ORDER BY t1.ord_total_amt DESC, t1.ord_id ASC
```

```sql

```

```sql
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(m.mv_ts, '%Y-%m') AS mv_month, SUM(ABS(m.qty)) AS total_units_out FROM inv_move m JOIN prod_catalog p ON m.sku = p.sku WHERE p.categ_cd = 'ELC' AND m.mv_type = 'OUT' AND m.mv_ts >= '2025-10-01' AND m.mv_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY mv_month ORDER BY mv_month ASC
```

Using a multi-step WITH clause: first aggregate refund requests by order ID to get the total refund per order, second compute the average of those totals, and finally list order IDs whose total refund is greater than that average. Output order ID and total refund.

```sql
WITH order_refund_totals AS (SELECT ord_id, SUM(rfd_amt) AS total_rfd FROM refund_req GROUP BY ord_id), avg_order_refund AS (SELECT AVG(total_rfd) AS mean_rfd FROM order_refund_totals) SELECT ord_id, total_rfd FROM order_refund_totals, avg_order_refund WHERE total_rfd > mean_rfd ORDER BY total_rfd DESC, ord_id ASC
```

```sql
SELECT e.emp_nm, cl.code_desc, COUNT(t.tkt_id) AS assigned_tkt_cnt FROM support_tkt t JOIN emp e ON t.assigned_emp_id = e.emp_id JOIN code_lookup cl ON e.dept_cd = cl.code_val AND cl.code_type = 'DEPT' WHERE t.opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY e.emp_id, e.emp_nm, cl.code_desc ORDER BY assigned_tkt_cnt DESC, e.emp_nm ASC
```

```sql

```

Calculate the percentage contribution of each warehouse's total inventory to the entire company's inventory sum. Show the warehouse ID, total stock, and percentage (rounded or as decimal), ordered by percentage descending.

```sql
WITH wh_sum AS (SELECT wh_id, SUM(on_hand_qty) AS stock FROM inventory GROUP BY wh_id), total_sum AS (SELECT SUM(on_hand_qty) AS tot FROM inventory) SELECT t.wh_id, t.stock, (t.stock * 100.0 / ts.tot) AS pct FROM wh_sum AS t CROSS JOIN total_sum AS ts ORDER BY pct DESC, t.wh_id ASC
```
